slides.headline: DIESEL HIT $8 A GALLON IN SOME STATES AFTER US-IRAN STRIKES ON THE WORLD'S MAIN OIL LANE
slides.image_prompt: SUBJECT: A hulking American commercial diesel semi-truck at a sun-baked truck stop, fuel nozzle driven deep into its tank — catastrophic, unstoppable. BACKDROP PROPS: A towering illuminated roadside diesel price board with a blazing red numeral on its white panel, a deep blood-orange sky cleaved by two rising columns of thick black oily smoke from the distant horizon. PALETTE: Deep orange and blood red. LABELS: "$8" on price board. INSET: circular bubble of dark military warships silhouetted on fire-lit open water. Documentary news photo, 35mm, slight film grain.

slides.headline: EVERY EXPERT SAID THE OIL LANES WOULD STAY OPEN
slides.body:
Even as US-Iran tensions dragged on all year, the assumption was simple: the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most critical oil chokepoint, would stay passable.

Then the strikes started.

slides.headline: DIESEL HIT $5.90 AND EVERY TRUCK IN AMERICA FELT IT
slides.body:
Every freight truck, farm vehicle, and delivery van in America runs on diesel. When diesel goes up, everything on a store shelf goes up.

Your grocery bill is the last stop on that chain.

slides.headline: $5.816, THE RECORD THAT JUST FELL
slides.body: $5.90 just broke it, diesel's new all-time US record

slides.headline: THE STRIKES STARTED AT THE WORST POSSIBLE MOMENT
slides.body:
US-Iran strikes hit at peak diesel demand, exactly when prices were already under pressure.

A huge share of the world's oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Your diesel costs are the collateral.

slides.headline: WHEN DIESEL SPIKES, EVERY BUSINESS PAYS MORE
slides.body: Hormuz carries 20% of global oil supply Strikes landed at peak US diesel demand Every delivery truck cost just went up No clear price ceiling while conflict runs

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: DIESEL JUST HIT AN ALL-TIME RECORD
slides.body: Diesel hit $5.90/gallon, first time in US history Some states already above $8.00/gallon US-Iran strikes hit during peak demand No clear price ceiling while conflict continues Send this to anyone filling a work truck.

caption:
Diesel just hit an all-time US record and it's coming for your wallet. Swipe to see why this one isn't going back down ⛽

The all-time diesel record above $5.90 a gallon, the assumption that oil shipping lanes would hold, what record pump prices do to every delivery truck and store shelf in America, the states already above $8 a gallon, the worst possible timing of US-Iran strikes landing at peak demand season, and why there's no price ceiling in sight.

When the world's biggest oil lane enters active conflict at peak demand, prices don't just spike, they break records. Every business that ships or delivers just absorbed a cost increase with no warning.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you how to stay ahead of fuel surcharges before they hit your invoices.

Sources: The Kobeissi Letter on X
